core_map.summary: Unconditional route around the canonical defect-span-three interface. Minimum counterexamples have defect span exactly three; opposite longest-path endpoint deletion covers always expose support/order disagreement. With positive deletion slack, every central deletion reduces to crossing, order disagreement, or same-slot replacement; comparing the two endpoint anchors shows that at most two central labels can remain same-slot from both ends. The general pair-deletion reconstruction lemma isolates the underlying reason: two distinct ordered block structures can be equalized by deleting at most two labels. Thus repeated clean replacement is no longer the main bulk obstruction. The current closure gap is to consume the resulting support crossings and order reversals into endpoint absorption or defect span at most two.
core_map.title: Defect-span three and deletion-cover compatibility give the canonical global obstruction interface

core_map.summary: Anchored four-window transport route: every deletion state is driven to a Hamiltonian four-window or bounded barrier, then repeated endpoint exchanges, five- and six-window amplification, and short label migration reduce nonescaping states to order disagreement, strict descent, or a coherent endpoint-square obstruction.
